Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. entry.title: Microsoft workers accuse company of trying to get customers "addicted" to AI while forcing it on their own staff and making them party to "human rights violations"
entry.summary: A group of "concerned Microsoft workers" have published an open letter criticising their employer's "speed-at-all-costs" approach to generative AI, which they argue is "harming our customers, colleagues, shareholders, vendors, and the planet". They accuse Microsoft leadership of trying to get people "addicted" to genAI, while making their own staff miserable by mandating AI usage. Echoing the on-going BDS campaign against Microsoft's Xbox business, the writers contend that Microsoft have become party to "human rights violations" by selling generative AI technology to Israel's military during the latter's invasion of Gaza, which a UN commission has deemed a genocide. They're also critical of Microsoft's contracts with the USA's draconian Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. While seemingly not against generative AI in principle, they're organising against "the AI industry’s trajectory to continue to enrich AI’s powerful few", pointing out that AI companies now account for a terrifying share of the global stock market. entry.title: DigiCert: únik zákaznických údajů
entry.summary:
Digicert hlásí neoprávněné čtení archivních zákaznických údajů. Došlo k němu po migraci z února 2025, po níž se interní systém, dříve dostupný jen přes VPN, stal přístupným z internetu. Chyba v oprávněních umožnila nově vytvořeným účtům číst archivní záznamy. K přístupu k datům mělo dojít mezi 27. červnem a 2. červencem 2026. DigiCert neoprávněné čtení potvrdil až 19. října 2026. Problém zpočátku vyhodnotil jako tvorbu účtů, ne jako přístup k datům.
Dotčené údaje zahrnovaly jména, pracovní e-maily, telefonní čísla a obchodní adresy. U malé části záznamů byly také doklady, například pasy, řidičské průkazy nebo účty za služby. Počet zasažených lidí ani organizací zatím zveřejněn nebyl. DigiCert podle zpráv stále posuzuje, komu se týkaly doklady, a informuje dotčené zákazníky. DigiCert uvádí, že jeho certifikační služby, CertCentral, DigiCert ONE, přihlašovací údaje zákazníků ani vydané certifikáty zasaženy nebyly. Nebyly zaznamenány změny validací ani vydávání či rušení certifikátů. Kvůli tomuto incidentu tedy zákazníci nemají měnit aktivní certifikáty. DigiCert přístup uzavřel, vypnul samoobslužnou registraci a přidal další kontroly. Pokud jste DigiCertu posílali doklad totožnosti, ověřte u svého kontaktního zástupce, zda se vás incident týká. Zprávy, které se odvolávají na incident a žádají heslo, ověřovací kód nebo opětovné nahrání dokladu, si ověřte nezávisle přes svůj účet či známý kontakt — samotná oznámení neuvádějí úplný seznam zasažených.

entry.title: Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it
entry.summary:
I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.
Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

entry.title: Oblivion and Skyrim’s gap was bridged by forward-looking books about a murderous floating island, so why is The Elder Scrolls 6 stuck reanimating a world that’s stood still since 2011
entry.summary: Long waits between mainline entries in a series aren’t a new phenomenon, if perhaps a bit more common nowadays due to big games' ballooning development cycles. It took about 23 years for BioWare’s Baldur's Gate 2 to be followed up by Larian’s Baldur’s Gate 3, though there were a decent amount of spin-offs and remasters peppered between the two. The wait for The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel hasn’t stretched on that long quite yet, but as Bethesda finally revealed concrete details about it just in time for Skyrim's 15th birthday, it really hit home for me that TES VI will be tasked with restoring motion to a world where calendars have been stuck in the 201st year of the 4th era since 2011. Perhaps it’s because I’m still in my twenties and haven’t lived long enough to see that many things I like pause their forward march for this long before returning. There’s also a good chance my expectations of timelines rolling forward on a regular basis without the need for a whole new entry are coloured by the constant stream of new stuff fed into most games via updates and live service passes these days. entry.title: Horror-steeped card game Forbidden Solitaire shows how a strong theme can elevate even decade-old mechanics
entry.summary: Like a tag team of oiled snakes that have entered a wrestling contest, theme is a difficult quality to pin down. A game can be well designed, but if it lacks a coherence between those mechanics and its appearance, narrative, and its framing, there is a dissonance that can be hard to ignore. I realise I've just stepped into an old argument by using the word 'dissonance', but Hocking was right, games that don't cohere can be jarring. A developer may desire that sensation of discomfort, but often it is accidental and unwanted. (Much like opening an article with a simile about wrestling snakes when there is nothing connecting that image to a game about solitaire. It might be a good line, but it doesn't smoothly connect with the rest of the article to elevate its argument.) Anyway, what does this all have to do with Forbidden Solitaire, a game in which you're delving deeper into a dungeon filled with horrors, progressing by clearing screens of cards? Well, it's an excellent example of how well-handled theming can raise a game into something more than its parts. Read more
